name: Pueblo of San Felipe grant, confirmed by Congress December 22, 1858 (Royce Area 666)
citation: Act of December 22, 1858, ch. 5, 11 Stat. 374 (confirmation); Act of June 7, 1924, 43 Stat. 636; Act of May 31, 1933, 48 Stat. 108
promises: Congress confirmed the Pueblo of San Felipe's land claim, as reported favorably by the Surveyor General of New Mexico, and ordered it surveyed and patented (Act of December 22, 1858, 11 Stat. 374).
The Act says the confirmation is only a relinquishment of the United States' own title and claim, and does not affect any adverse valid rights.
Royce records the grant as 34,766.86 acres, a Spanish grant of 1689 patented in 1864.

The Pueblo Lands Act of 1924 made the United States liable, and directed the Pueblo Lands Board to award compensation, for Pueblo land and water lost through the United States' failure to seasonably prosecute the Pueblo's rights (Section 6).

breaches.what: Under the Pueblo Lands Act of 1924, title to land claimed by non-Indians within the Pueblo of San Felipe's lands was extinguished in their favour. The Act of May 31, 1933 names the Pueblo of San Felipe among the pueblos from which lands and water rights were divested under the 1924 Act.

breaches.what: Congress authorized $14,954.53 for the Pueblo of San Felipe 'in addition to the awards made by the Pueblo Lands Board', in payment of the liability of the United States to the Pueblo declared by the 1924 Act. The Indian Claims Commission later described these 1933 sums as Congress finding the Board's awards unfair.

compensation: The Pueblo Lands Board made an award under Section 6 of the 1924 Act (amount not read in this pass). The Act of May 31, 1933 authorized a further $14,954.53 for the Pueblo of San Felipe, to be spent by the Secretary of the Interior with the Pueblo's approval on replacement lands, water rights or permanent improvements, in three annual instalments from fiscal year 1937. Section 6 of that Act let a pueblo accept the sums in full discharge of its claims under the 1924 Act. The Indian Claims Commission wrote in 1977 that in most cases the Board awarded only a fraction of fair market value and that Congress, finding the Board unfair, paid the difference except in a few instances.

openQuestions: The date 1886-10-01 in treaties.json is not an event date for this land. Royce prints the Pueblo grants under a block headed 'Oct. 1, Act of Congress, Stat. L. XI, 374'; 11 Stat. 374 is the Act of December 22, 1858, which confirmed the grant. This is land the Pueblo kept, not land it ceded. Not edited.

The 1933 Act gives one sum for the Pueblo of San Felipe and does not split it by tract. Section 6 of the 1924 Act covers only land inside the exterior boundaries of land granted or confirmed to a pueblo, so the sum relates to confirmed grant land, but this pass did not read the Pueblo Lands Board's own report on this Pueblo to confirm the acreage lost inside this grant (Royce's area) as against any other confirmed or purchased tract.
Whether the Pueblo of San Felipe elected under Section 6 of the 1933 Act to accept the sum in full discharge, and when it was actually appropriated and paid, was not researched.
The Pueblo of San Felipe's own account was not located (sanfelipepueblo.org did not answer). Whether San Felipe held other confirmed or purchased land in 1924 was not checked.
The statute link in treaties.json (ops.libs.uga.edu) was not used; the Act was read on govinfo.
today: The grant remains the Pueblo's land base. Land and water inside it that passed to non-Indians under the 1924 Act was compensated, not returned; the 1933 Act directed the money to replacement land, water and improvements.

plain.promised: In 1858 Congress confirmed the Pueblo of San Felipe's land grant and later issued a patent, giving up only the United States' own claim to it.
plain.happened: Under the Pueblo Lands Act of 1924, land held by non-Indians inside the Pueblo's lands was confirmed to them. In 1933 Congress named the Pueblo and authorized $14,954.53 more than the Pueblo Lands Board had awarded.
plain.today: The land that passed to non-Indians was not returned; the 1933 money was for replacement land, water and improvements.
